subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the Gersmehl model for tropical rainforests, the largest nutrient store is:
questions.explain: In rainforests rapid uptake and dense vegetation mean most nutrients are held in the biomass store.

questions.q: UK heather moorland maintained by regular burning and sheep grazing is an example of a:
questions.explain: Heather moorland is a plagioclimax kept in place by management practices that prevent woodland regeneration.

questions.q: Which strategy best combines ecological and economic sustainability in rainforest management?
options: Ecotourism and agroforestry that generate income while conserving the forest
Total exclusion of all human use
questions.explain: Ecotourism and agroforestry provide livelihoods while keeping the forest largely intact, balancing conservation with development.

questions.q: An arresting factor in succession is one that:
options: Halts or deflects succession, preventing the climatic climax
questions.explain: Arresting factors, such as grazing, fire or trampling, stop succession reaching its natural climax.

questions.q: Rapid nutrient cycling in tropical rainforests means that when forest is cleared, the soil:
options: Quickly loses fertility because nutrients were stored in biomass, not soil
questions.explain: Because most nutrients are held in vegetation and recycled fast, removing the trees and leaching soon leaves infertile soil.

questions.q: A psammosere is a succession that begins on:
questions.explain: A psammosere develops on sand, typically coastal dunes.

questions.q: The savanna (tropical grassland) biome is defined climatically by:
options: A marked wet and dry season
questions.explain: Savanna grasslands experience distinct wet and dry seasons, favouring grasses with scattered trees.

questions.q: In savanna grasslands, periodic fire acts as:
options: A nutrient sink that removes all minerals permanently
An arresting factor that maintains grassland by limiting tree growth
questions.explain: Regular fires suppress tree saplings and recycle nutrients, helping maintain the grassland as a fire (plagio)climax.

questions.q: Net primary productivity (NPP) is calculated as:
questions.explain: NPP is gross primary productivity minus the energy lost through plant respiration, i.e. the energy available to consumers.

questions.q: Selective logging is considered more sustainable than clear-felling because it:
options: Takes only certain trees, allowing forest structure and regeneration to remain
questions.explain: Removing only selected mature trees maintains canopy and soil structure, allowing the forest to regenerate.

questions.q: The climatic climax community is the:
options: Stable end-point community in equilibrium with the regional climate
questions.explain: The climatic climax is the self-sustaining community in equilibrium with the prevailing climate.

questions.q: The high biodiversity of tropical rainforests is largely explained by:
options: Stable, high energy availability and many ecological niches
questions.explain: Consistent warmth, light and moisture sustain high productivity and a wide range of niches, supporting many species.

questions.q: Decomposers (detritivores and saprotrophs) are essential to ecosystems because they:
options: Break down dead organic matter, recycling nutrients into the soil store
questions.explain: Decomposers release nutrients locked in dead matter back into the soil, sustaining the nutrient cycle.

questions.q: The establishment of a marine protected area is an example of which conservation approach?
questions.explain: Protecting species within their natural habitat is in-situ conservation, contrasting with ex-situ methods like zoos or seed banks.

questions.q: In an ecosystem, gross primary productivity (GPP) refers to:
options: Energy lost at each trophic transfer
The total rate at which producers fix energy through photosynthesis
questions.explain: GPP is the total rate of energy capture by autotrophs before any is used in respiration.

questions.q: In the Gersmehl nutrient-cycling model, the three stores of nutrients are:
questions.explain: Gersmehl represents nutrient cycling between three stores: biomass, litter and soil.

questions.q: Energy enters most ecosystems and flows in which direction?
options: It flows one way from the Sun through trophic levels and is lost as heat
It flows from consumers to producers
It is recycled endlessly like nutrients
questions.explain: Unlike nutrients, energy flows unidirectionally from sunlight through producers and consumers and is ultimately lost as heat.

questions.q: A plagioclimax is a community that:
options: Reaches its natural climatic climax undisturbed
Is held below climatic climax by continued human interference
questions.explain: A plagioclimax results from ongoing human interference (e.g. grazing, burning) that arrests succession below the natural climax.

questions.q: Pioneer species in primary succession are characterised by their ability to:
options: Tolerate harsh conditions and begin soil formation
questions.explain: Pioneers such as lichens and mosses tolerate extreme conditions and start building soil for later species.

questions.q: Deforestation of tropical rainforest contributes to climate change mainly by:
options: Increasing the albedo of the planet only
Releasing stored carbon and reducing the forest's carbon sink capacity
questions.explain: Clearing and burning forest releases stored carbon dioxide and removes a major carbon sink, enhancing the greenhouse effect.

questions.q: Primary succession differs from secondary succession because primary succession:
options: Begins on a previously vegetated surface after disturbance
Begins on a newly exposed surface with no pre-existing soil or seed bank
questions.explain: Primary succession starts on bare, lifeless surfaces (e.g. bare rock, new lava) lacking soil, whereas secondary succession follows disturbance of an already-soiled area.

questions.q: Biodiversity is best defined as:
options: The number of trophic levels only
The variety of species, genetic and habitat diversity within an area
questions.explain: Biodiversity encompasses species, genetic and ecosystem/habitat variety.

questions.q: Which of the following is a regulating ecosystem service?
options: Climate and flood regulation through carbon storage and interception
questions.explain: Regulating services include climate control, water and flood regulation and pollination, distinct from provisioning, supporting and cultural services.

questions.q: In a Gersmehl diagram, the flow of nutrients from litter to soil represents:
questions.explain: Decomposition releases nutrients from the litter store into the soil store.

questions.q: Tropical rainforests occur in a distribution mainly:
options: In a belt near the Equator where it is hot and wet year-round
questions.explain: Rainforests are concentrated in the equatorial zone with consistently high temperatures and rainfall.

questions.q: A biome is best described as:
options: A single population of one species
A large-scale community of plants and animals adapted to a particular climate
questions.explain: A biome is a global-scale ecosystem type defined by its climate and characteristic vegetation and fauna.

questions.q: A succession that develops on bare rock is specifically termed a:
questions.explain: A lithosere is the succession beginning on a bare rock surface.

questions.q: A complete sequence of seral stages in a particular succession is called a:
questions.explain: A sere is the full set of seral stages from pioneer community to climax.

questions.q: Roughly what proportion of energy is typically transferred from one trophic level to the next?
questions.explain: Only around 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level; the rest is lost mainly through respiration, heat and waste.
